terms.comment: In rhetoric, Greek ἔμφασις: saying less than one leaves to be understood (Lewis & Short). Its other senses are a sign or indication, applause, and the meaning of a word (see mean).

phrases.latin: significātiō est, quae plūs in suspīciōne relinquit, quam positum est in ōrātiōne
phrases.english: implication is what leaves more to be suspected than has been put into words

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
